lines.text: How many pairs are exactly five units apart?
lines.caption: How many pairs are exactly five units apart?

lines.text: The dots are one unit apart, in rows and columns.
lines.caption: The dots are one unit apart, in rows and columns.

lines.text: Count the pairs of dots that are exactly five units apart.
lines.caption: Count the pairs of dots that are exactly five units apart.

lines.text: A row of five dots is only four units long. So five has to be a slant!
lines.caption: A row of five dots is only four units long. So five has to be a slant!

lines.text: Three across and four down is a three, four, five triangle.
lines.caption: Three across and four down is a three, four, five triangle.

lines.text: It fits in two spots, and there are four different slants.
lines.caption: It fits in two spots, and there are four different slants.

lines.text: Four slants, two spots each. That makes eight pairs!
lines.caption: Four slants, two spots each. That makes eight pairs!

lines.text: Sixteen is the trap. It counts every pair twice.
lines.caption: Sixteen is the trap. It counts every pair twice.

lines.text: Why does each slant fit twice? The full lesson shows two neat ways, plus every trap.
